review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions of cubeSet, openCubeSet and cubeScaleFactor in TriadicCube.lean. I also grepped for uses of the simp lemmas and of the duplicated positivity lemma. I did not find a credible rewrite cycle. descendantsAtScale_pred looks fine: it is oriented toward the simpler childCubes, and its LHS does not clash with descendantsAtScale_self. The two findings are both about the interface and are not experimentally verified. I cannot run Lean, so the simp behaviour described below is inferred from the lemma statements and the default simp set. The effect on downstream proofs outside this directory was not checked.

findings.problem: Both membership lemmas are @[simp] and are meant to be used together. `mem_cubeBoundaryLayer_iff` rewrites `x ∈ cubeBoundaryLayer Q t` to `x ∈ cubeSet Q ∧ x ∉ cubeShrunkSet Q t`. `mem_cubeShrunkSet_iff` then expands the inner membership into the raw coordinate inequalities under a negation. The default simp set then probably pushes the negation through (`not_forall`, `not_and`, `not_lt`). That would leave an `∃ i, … → …` formula in a messy normal form. The expansion is also asymmetric. `cubeSet` and `openCubeSet` have no simp membership lemma in the target or in TriadicCube.lean, apart from the originCube and translateCube variants, so the cube itself stays opaque while the shrunk set is unfolded. The file's own proofs avoid the interface and unfold by hand (`simp [cubeShrunkSet, cubeSet]`, `intro hxt; exact hx_not_mem …`).
findings.proposed_change: Remove @[simp] from `mem_cubeShrunkSet_iff`, so that `x ∈ cubeShrunkSet Q t` stays as an atom. Keep `mem_cubeBoundaryLayer_iff` and `mem_cubeBoundary_iff` as simp lemmas, so the boundary layer reduces to `x ∈ cubeSet Q ∧ x ∉ cubeShrunkSet Q t`. Provide the coordinatewise form as a non-simp lemma for explicit `rw`/`simp only`. If a fully expanded normal form is wanted instead, add matching `mem_cubeSet_iff` and `mem_openCubeSet_iff` simp lemmas so that all three sets expand uniformly.
findings.benefit: Simp goals involving boundary layers stay readable and stable. Users can combine `cubeShrunkSet_zero`, `cubeShrunkSet_anti` and `cubeShrunkSet_eq_empty_iff` with the membership lemma without the shrunk set being unfolded first.

findings.excerpt:
theorem BoundaryLayer.cubeScaleFactor_pos {d : ℕ} (Q : TriadicCube d) : 0 < cubeScaleFactor Q := by
  simpa [cubeScaleFactor] using (zpow_pos (show (0 : ℝ) < 3 by norm_num) Q.scale)
findings.problem: The canonical positivity fact for `cubeScaleFactor` is missing from the file that defines it. It is proved twice, as `BoundaryLayer.cubeScaleFactor_pos` here and as `CubeMeasure.cubeScaleFactor_pos` in CubeMeasure.lean. Neither copy is a simp lemma. Each use manually does `have hscale_pos := BoundaryLayer.cubeScaleFactor_pos Q` and then feeds it to nlinarith or le_of_lt. A fact like `0 < cubeScaleFactor Q` or `cubeScaleFactor Q ≠ 0` cannot be discharged automatically as a side condition in rewriting. The simp set only has `cubeScaleFactor_originCube` and `cubeScaleFactor_translateCube`.
findings.proposed_change: Put a single `cubeScaleFactor_pos` in TriadicCube.lean next to `cubeScaleFactor`, tagged @[simp] (and optionally `.ne'` and `.le` variants, or a positivity extension). Delete the two namespaced copies and use the shared lemma here, for example in `cubeShrunkSet_anti` and the `nlinarith` proofs.
findings.benefit: Simp and positivity can discharge scale-factor side goals automatically. There is one canonical lemma instead of two parallel private-style duplicates, so later geometry files do not reprove it.
